why: THE FLIP WHITELIST: the backend symbols the boundary may still carry when --require-zero runs.
Every entry is a symbol that is PRESENT in the measured set TODAY, with the reason it is still
there and what removes it. The list may only SHRINK: an entry with no live hit is a failure
(the exception it claims no longer exists, so it must be deleted), and --update never touches this
file. A symbol that is not on this list and not in the measured set is nothing; a measured symbol
that is not on this list fails the gate.
MEASURED TODAY: 3 symbols / 11 reference sites, and 41 engine+application files still import a
module deren_vulkan owns (the import check below reports it) - the layer the symbol count cannot
see, and the reason the flip is not imminent.

entries.reason: initializer for module deren.vulkan.core. 9 engine files still import a deren_vulkan module (acceleration_structure, filters, goo_rim, toon_screen_rim, pipelines, primitive, ray_tracing, readback, runtime.declarations), and importing a backend module forces its initializer. LEAVES WITH: the dynamic-link runtime plus the constant_init/core.pipeline imports the passes still carry - i.e. when the import check reads 0.

core::core(rhi::create_info const&). The engine still CONSTRUCTS the concrete backend class (runtime.constructor's std::make_shared<core>). LEAVES WITH: the dynamic-link runtime, which constructs through deren_make_api_core(rhi::abi_version, &options, &error_info) into a shared_ptr<rhi::api_core> and never names core.

vk_sampler::operator*() const. The engine still dereferences the backend's shared samplers (the renderer's sampler set) to reach the native VkSampler. LEAVES WITH: a small batch that reaches those samplers through the contract (create_sampler + vulkan_escape::native_sampler), which is NOT the dynamic-link runtime's job.
